A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDA/CDA-M research, with matching core equations, models, datasets, and experimental framework. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support a reliable comparison; visual inspection resolved extraction difficulties.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA and RAG experiments, calibration and momentum ablations, entropy-distribution measurements, and generation case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original QA and RAG results, three-seed summaries, trained-comparator experiments, ablations, output-distribution analyses, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed combination of parametric, contextual, and abstention distributions, null-prompt entropy calibration, and momentum update remains mathematically and procedurally unchanged. Renumbered equations, reordered template arguments, and expanded explanations do not establish a changed CDA algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MRQA NQ, HotpotQA, and TriviaQA, the same four knowledge-access conditions, and single-context Wikipedia RAG. The new training and transfer comparisons reuse these datasets and QA tasks; their source-target training design changes evaluation procedures within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds ENTROPY thresholding, including first-token, average, maximum, and minimum variants, to the controlled and RAG comparisons. It also evaluates instruction-tuned abstention models and a RoBERTa-base external verifier in Section 6.4 and Appendix C.3. These substantially broaden v1's prompting and decoding comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces within-dataset and cross-dataset training/evaluation protocols, validation-RS selection over learning rates and training epochs, and train-set-RS selection of entropy thresholds. Appendix D adds a 100-sample timing experiment. The existing two-shot greedy QA evaluation, knowledge-estimation thresholds, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds generalization analyses of trained comparators, two first-token output-distribution case studies in Section 6.6, and computational-cost analysis in Appendix D. Conversely, v1's entropy-histogram diagnostic in Section 4 and Appendix B is removed. Calibration and momentum analyses remain, including the two existing generation cases.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without specifying an experimental seed count or reporting dispersion. v2 explicitly reports three-seed averages, per-seed dataset sizes in Table 4, and standard deviations in Tables 6, 7, and 10–13. This establishes substantially expanded statistical reporting, without establishing how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: Main and calibration results are revised, and entropy, trained-comparator, output-probability, and runtime results are added. For example, LLAMA3 8B INSTRUCT CDA-M TriviaQA F1ans changes from 78.77 to a reported three-seed mean of 80.93 in Table 1; the aggregation conditions differ. All retained-method RAG scores match between v1 Table 8 and v2 Table 9.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds a computational-cost derivation using template, context, and query lengths, approximating the five inference costs by 2 O(Lc^2) when context length dominates. The existing knowledge definitions, CDA equations, and metric formulas remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim of training-free, knowledge-sensitive answering and abstention remains. v2 adds an introduction-level claim of robust generalization relative to training-based methods and foregrounds the controlled testbed as a contribution in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 interprets trained comparators' transfer weaknesses as domain specialization and adds explanations of how output probabilities illustrate knowledge amplification and abstention. It expands the computational-cost tradeoff discussion while retaining the single-context, short-form QA limitations. The detailed interpretation of v1's entropy histograms is removed, but the central calibration and momentum explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents entropy-threshold selection, the RoBERTa-base verifier and MLP head, QLoRA/PEFT settings with rank 4 and alpha 16, learning-rate and epoch searches, and RTX 3090 timing conditions. These substantially expand reproducibility information. v1's explicit exclusion of answer-containing distractor candidates is no longer documented, without establishing that the underlying filtering changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature supporting entropy thresholding, verification, and training comparisons, including Huang et al. (2025), Cobbe et al. (2021), Cohen et al. (2023, 2024), and Yang et al. (2024). It removes Cheng et al. (2024) and several hallucination references. The central positioning within contrastive decoding and abstention research remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around the controlled testbed. The standalone uncertainty-analysis section disappears, entropy definitions move into the method section, and the appendices are reorganized around testbed, implementation, ablation, and cost details. These constitute substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 moves the four-scenario schematic to the opening, adds a dataset-construction flowchart, consolidates three prompt tables into Figure 3, and reorganizes Table 1 with models across columns. It removes the entropy histograms and radar charts, redraws retained case studies and momentum plots, and adds output-distribution, training, timing, and statistical displays.

improvement.justification: The added comparators, three-seed variability reporting, training details, and measured runtime improve empirical scrutiny beyond v1's narrower comparisons and point estimates. These gains are tempered by removal of the entropy diagnostic and new reporting errors: Figure 9(b) repeats NQ curves under HotpotQA, Table 6 reverses the F1 headers relative to Table 2, and TriviaQA-to-NQ instruction-tuning RS is 57.70 in Table 3 but 59.70 in Table 7. These problems limit the overall quality gain.
